newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-CERA bank buys Banque Indosuez Belgique.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CERA bank buys Banque Indosuez Belgique.

text.p: CERA Bank, Belgium's sixth-largest bank, said on Friday it would buy 80 percent of Banque Indosuez Belgique from French Banque Indosuez.
"We had been trying for quite some time to improve our place on the banking scene," CERA chief executive officer Willy Breesch told a news conference.

He declined to give financial details of the basic agreement, signed on Thursday, but expected the agreement to be finalised by April at the latest after approval by authorities and due diligence procedures.

Indosuez Belgique, 99.8 percent owned by its French namesake, will become the investment arm of the CERA group but maintains its autonomy. It will continue to get operational support from its French former parent, Breesch said.
He said the workforce at both CERA, a retail bank which focuses on the agricultural sector, and Indosuez Belgique would not be affected by the takeover.
"CERA has 950 branches but there is virtually no overlap of commercial networks. Moreover (the banks) are aiming at different target audiences," said Breesch.
Indosuez Belgique is mainly involved on the financial markets and with small and medium-sized enterprises. It has branches in five major Belgian cities.
The remainder of Indosuez Belgique stays in the hands on Banque Indosuez apart from the 0.2 percent not held by the French bank which stays in public hands.
Breesch said CERA would wait for the publication of a new Belgian law which would no longer force it to make a public bid for the small 0.2 percent stake.
"We will use this law as soon as it becomes operational to prevent us from having to make a public bid," he said.
Indosuez Belgique specialises in capital markets, corporate and private banking, asset-based and corporate finance.
"We are determined to develop all of these skills," Breesch said. "We can improve CERA's position but the deal will also be positive for Indosuez Belqique," he said.
French Compagnie de Suez has sold 51 percent of Banque Indosuez to French bank Credit Agricole and is due to sell it a further 29 percent in July 1997.
At the end of June 1996 CERA had total assets of 1,241 billion Belgian francs ($39.1 billion). It had a 1995 consolidated net profit of 3.376 billion francs ($106.5 million).
Indosuez Belgique had assets worth 225 billion francs ($7.1 billion) at the end of 1995 and earned a 418 million franc ($13.2 million) net profit.
